summary: Shannon County lookout on Tram Ridge, begun in 1938 and recorded at about 75 ft by NGS in 1962 and 1978; the Central US record says removed, with no date.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower with an enclosed observation room at the top
facts.status_note: The Central US Lookouts record marks the tower as removed, with no date. The last survey recovery found on the tower apex was in 1978.

events.note: Work began on the Tram Ridge site in February 1938. The Possum Trot tower was torn down and re-erected there, per a 1938 local paper.
Willie Martin and his wife moved from Tram Tower to High Tower, per a July 1940 local paper.
U.S. Coast and Geodetic Survey described the station on the tower top: four-legged steel structure with an enclosed observation room, about 75 feet high.
NGS recovered the station at the apex of the tower, described as a four-legged structure about 75 feet high, condition good.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1938 paper puts the tower 4 miles southwest of Winona. The 1962 survey puts it about 3 miles southwest of Winona. Both are approximate. The NGS coordinates are within about 50 m of the brief's coordinates.

notes_for_editor: The gone status rests on one undated Removed label. No source gives a removal date or describes the site today. The NGS datasheet's last recorded recovery is 1978. The 1938 and 1940 items are read through the Central US Lookouts page, not the original newspapers.
